book.t: In the Hebrew text 1:18-21 is 2:1-4, and 2:1-13 is 2:5-17.

1:1.t: The eighth month of Darius's second year was October-November 520 BC. Zechariah began prophesying two months after Haggai, encouraging the rebuilding of the temple.

1:8.t: "Brown": the KJV's "speckled"; the color is uncertain.

1:20.t: "Craftsmen": the KJV's "carpenters", smiths or skilled workers.

2:8.t: "After the Glorious One has sent me": the KJV's "After the glory hath he sent me". The Hebrew is difficult.
"Whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye": the pupil of the eye, the most sensitive and protected part. God guards His people that closely (Deuteronomy 32:10).

4:10.t: The KJV's source text adds a marginal note ("shall rejoice") to this verse, not part of the verse.

4:14.t: "The two who are anointed": literally "the two sons of oil", probably Joshua the priest and Zerubbabel the governor.

5:2.t: "About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide": the KJV's "twenty cubits ... ten cubits".

5:6.t: "A basket": the KJV's "an ephah", a basket the size of the ephah measure, about 22 liters. "The iniquity of the people": the KJV's "their resemblance"; the Hebrew reads "their eye", and the Greek and Syriac "their iniquity".

5:7.t: "The cover of lead": the KJV's "a talent of lead", a heavy lead lid.

6:3.t: "Dappled": the KJV's "grisled and bay". "All of them powerful": the Hebrew amutstsim, which the KJV renders "bay".

6:6.t: "After them": following the KJV and the Hebrew; some read "toward the west".

6:11.t: "Crowns": the Hebrew is plural, perhaps one elaborate crown of several bands.

6:14.t: "Helem": following the KJV and the Hebrew; probably the same man as Heldai in verse 10. "Hen" means "gracious one", perhaps a title of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

7:1.t: The fourth year of Darius: December 518 BC. "Kislev": the KJV's "Chisleu".

7:3.t: The fast of the fifth month mourned the burning of the temple (2 Kings 25:8-9); the fast of the seventh month mourned the murder of Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:1-3).

7:7.t: "The Negev and the western foothills": the KJV's "the south and the plain".

8:19.t: The fasts of the fourth and tenth months recalled the breaching of Jerusalem's walls and the start of the siege.

9:1.t: Hadrach was a region in Syria.

10:1.t: "In the springtime": the KJV's "in the time of the latter rain".

10:3.t: "The leaders": the KJV's "the goats", the lead animals of a flock.

10:4.t: "Cornerstone ... tent peg ... battle bow": pictures of strong leaders who will come from Judah.

11:13.t: "To the potter": the KJV's reading. The Syriac reads "into the treasury".

12:11.t: Hadad Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo: probably the mourning for King Josiah, killed at Megiddo (2 Chronicles 35:22-25).

13:5.t: "The land has been my livelihood since my youth": the KJV's "man taught me to keep cattle from my youth".

14:5.t: "By My mountain valley": the KJV's "to the valley of the mountains". "With you": the KJV's reading; some Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek read "with Him".

14:6.t: "Neither sunlight nor cold, frosty darkness": the KJV's "the light shall not be clear, nor dark". The Hebrew is difficult.

14:8.t: "The Dead Sea ... the Mediterranean Sea": the KJV's "the former sea ... the hinder sea".

14:10.t: "Like the Arabah": the KJV's "as a plain".

14:16.t: "The Festival of Tabernacles": the KJV's "the feast of tabernacles", or Booths (Leviticus 23:33-43).

14:21.t: "Canaanite": the Hebrew can also mean "merchant". Compare John 2:16.

1:3.t: "Return to Me ... and I will return to you": God invites repentance with a promise. Compare Malachi 3:7 and James 4:8.

3:1.t: "Satan" (Hebrew hassatan): "the accuser", standing to accuse the high priest. God Himself silences the accusation and replaces the filthy garments with clean ones, a picture of forgiveness. Compare Romans 8:33-34 and Revelation 12:10.

3:8.t: "My servant, the Branch" (Hebrew tsemach): see Isaiah 4:2, 11:1 and Jeremiah 23:5. The Messiah is both servant and branch of David's line.

4:6.t: "Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit" (Hebrew ki im beruchi): the temple would be finished not by human strength but by God's Spirit.

6:12.t: "The man whose name is the Branch ... a priest on His throne": in the Old Testament the offices of priest and king were kept separate. This prophecy unites them in one person. Hebrews 5-7 presents Jesus as the King-Priest in the order of Melchizedek. Following this reading, the Branch's pronouns are capitalized.

7:9.t: "Show steadfast love and compassion" (Hebrew hesed verachamim): God wants His people's fasting to be shown in justice and kindness. Compare Isaiah 58.

8:23.t: "Ten people from all languages and nations will take firm hold of one Jew": the nations will come to know God through His people.

9:9.t: "Your King comes to you ... humble and riding on a donkey": not on a warhorse but on a donkey, the animal of peace. Jesus fulfilled this deliberately when He entered Jerusalem (Matthew 21:4-5, John 12:14-15). Following this reading, the King's pronouns are capitalized in verses 9-10.

9:11.t: "The blood of My covenant": compare Exodus 24:8 and Jesus' words at the Last Supper (Mark 14:24).

11:12.t: "Thirty pieces of silver ... throw them to the potter": the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32), an insulting wage for God's shepherd. Matthew 27:9-10 sees this fulfilled when Judas threw back his thirty pieces of silver and the priests used them to buy the potter's field.

12:10.t: "They will look on Me, the one they have pierced, and they will mourn for Him": a striking change from "Me" to "Him", as though God Himself is the One pierced. John 19:37 applies the verse to Jesus on the cross, and Revelation 1:7 to His return. "A spirit of grace and supplication": God's Spirit brings repentance.

13:1.t: "A fountain ... to cleanse them from sin": compare Ezekiel 36:25 and 1 John 1:7.

13:7.t: "Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered": Jesus quoted this verse on the night He was arrested, when His disciples fled (Matthew 26:31). "The man who is close to Me" (Hebrew gever amiti): literally "the man who is My associate", one who stands beside God as an equal. Following this reading, the Shepherd's pronouns are capitalized.

14:4.t: "His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives": the angels at Jesus' ascension from the Mount of Olives promised that He would return in the same way (Acts 1:11-12).

14:9.t: "The LORD will be king over the whole earth ... one LORD, and His name the only name": echoing the Shema (Deuteronomy 6:4).

14:20.t: "Holy to the LORD": the words engraved on the high priest's turban (Exodus 28:36) will be written on ordinary things. In God's kingdom everything is set apart for Him.
